Question: Let \(T>0\), \(\mathbb R^+=(0,\infty)\), and \(s>\tfrac34\). Suppose \(u_0\in H^s(\mathbb R^+)\) and \(f\in H^{\frac{s+1}{3}}_{loc}(\mathbb R^+)\) satisfy the required compatibility conditions at \((x,t)=(0,0)\), where \(H^{\alpha}_{loc}(\mathbb R^+)\) denotes the local Sobolev space on \(\mathbb R^+\). For the initial-boundary value problem
\[
\begin{cases}
\partial_t u+\partial_x(\partial_x^2u+u^2)=0, & (x,t)\in \mathbb R^+\times(0,T),\\
u(x,0)=u_0(x), & x\in \mathbb R^+,\\
u(0,t)=f(t), & t\in(0,T),
\end{cases}
\]
what is the strongest statement that can be proved about existence and uniqueness of solutions to this IBVP?
Predicted label: 'D'
Predicted text: 'There exists exactly one solution \\(u\\) to this IBVP such that\n\\[\nu\\in C\\bigl((0,T);H^s(\\mathbb R^+)\\bigr)\\cap L^2\\bigl(0,T;H^{s+1}_{loc}(\\mathbb R^+)\\bigr).\n\\]'
Correct label: 'D'
Correct text: 'There exists exactly one solution \\(u\\) to this IBVP such that\n\\[\nu\\in C\\bigl((0,T);H^s(\\mathbb R^+)\\bigr)\\cap L^2\\bigl(0,T;H^{s+1}_{loc}(\\mathbb R^+)\\bigr).\n\\]'
Exact Match: 1.0
